references.name: Blockquotes
references.description: To create a blockquote, add a `>` in front of a paragraph.

examples.markdown: > Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle.
examples.html: Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle.

additional_examples.name: Blockquotes with Multiple Paragraphs
additional_examples.description: Blockquotes can contain multiple paragraphs. Add a `>` on the blank lines between the paragraphs.
additional_examples.markdown:
> Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle.

>

> The Witch bade her clean the pots and kettles and sweep the floor and keep the fire fed with wood.
additional_examples.html:
Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle.

The Witch bade her clean the pots and kettles and sweep the floor and keep the fire fed with wood.

additional_examples.name: Nested Blockquotes
additional_examples.description: Blockquotes can be nested. Add a `>>` in front of the paragraph you want to nest.
additional_examples.markdown:
> Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle.

>

>> The Witch bade her clean the pots and kettles and sweep the floor and keep the fire fed with wood.
additional_examples.html:
Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle.

The Witch bade her clean the pots and kettles and sweep the floor and keep the fire fed with wood.

additional_examples.name: Blockquotes with Other Elements
additional_examples.description: Blockquotes can contain other Markdown formatted elements. Not all elements can be used — you'll need to experiment to see which ones work.
additional_examples.markdown:
> ### The quarterly results look great!

>

> - Revenue was off the chart.

> - Profits were higher than ever.

>

>  *Everything* is going according to **plan**.
additional_examples.html:
The quarterly results look great!

  • Revenue was off the chart.
  • Profits were higher than ever.

Everything is going according to plan.

references.name: Bold
references.description: To bold text, add two asterisks or underscores before and after a word or phrase. To bold the middle of a word for emphasis, add two asterisks without spaces around the letters.

examples.markdown: I just love **bold text**.
I just love __bold text__.
Love**is**bold

references.name: Code
references.description: To denote a word or phrase as code, enclose it in tick marks (`` ` ``).

examples.markdown: At the command prompt, type `nano`.

additional_examples.name: Escaping Tick Marks
additional_examples.description: If the word or phrase you want to denote as code includes one or more tick marks, you can escape it by enclosing the word or phrase in double tick marks (``).

additional_examples.name: Code Blocks
additional_examples.description: To create code blocks, indent every line of the block by at least four spaces or one tab.

references.name: Headings
references.description: To create a heading, add number signs (`#`) in front of a word or phrase. The number of number signs you use should correspond to the heading level. For example, to create a heading level three (`<h3>`), use three number signs (e.g., `### My Header`).

examples.markdown: # Heading level 1
## Heading level 2
### Heading level 3
#### Heading level 4
##### Heading level 5
###### Heading level 6

additional_examples.name: Alternative H1 Syntax
additional_examples.description: Alternatively, on the line below the text, add any number of == characters for heading level 1.

additional_examples.name: Alternative H2 Syntax
additional_examples.description: Alternatively, on the line below the text, add any number of -- characters for heading level 2.

references.name: Horizontal Rules
references.description: To create a horizontal rule, use three or more asterisks (`***`), dashes (`---`), or underscores (`___`) on a line by themselves.

references.name: Images
references.description: To add an image, add an exclamation mark (`!`), followed by alt text in brackets, and the path or URL to the image asset in parentheses. You can optionally add a title after the URL in the parentheses.

examples.markdown: ![Philadelphia's Magic Gardens. This place was so cool!](/assets/images/philly-magic-gardens.jpg "Philadelphia's Magic Gardens")

additional_examples.name: Linking Images
additional_examples.description: To add a link to an image, enclose the Markdown for the image in brackets, and then add the link in parentheses.
additional_examples.markdown: [![An old rock in the desert](/assets/images/shiprock.jpg "Shiprock, New Mexico by Beau Rogers")](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1556010334-d6ed191db491?ixlib=rb-1.2.1&ixid=MnwxMjA3fDB8MHxzZWFyY2h8M3x8cm9ja3xlbnwwfHwwfHw%3D&auto=format&fit=crop&w=900&q=60)

references.name: Italic
references.description: To italicize text, add one asterisk or underscore before and after a word or phrase. To italicize the middle of a word for emphasis, add one asterisk without spaces around the letters.

examples.markdown: Italicized text is the *cat's meow*.
Italicized text is the _cat's meow_.
A*cat*meow

references.name: Line Breaks
references.description:
To create a line break (`
`), end a line with two or more spaces, and then type return.

examples.markdown:
This is the first line.  
And this is the second line.
examples.html:
This is the first line.
And this is the second line.

references.name: Links
references.description: To create a link, enclose the link text in brackets (e.g., `[Duck Duck Go]`) and then follow it immediately with the URL in parentheses (e.g., `(https://duckduckgo.com)`). You can optionally add a title after the URL in the parentheses.

examples.markdown: My favorite search engine is [Duck Duck Go](https://duckduckgo.com "The best search engine for privacy").
examples.html: My favorite search engine is Duck Duck Go.

additional_examples.name: URLs and Email Addresses
additional_examples.description: To quickly turn a URL or email address into a link, enclose it in angle brackets.

additional_examples.name: Formatting Links
additional_examples.description: To emphasize links, add asterisks before and after the brackets and parentheses.
additional_examples.markdown: I love supporting **[EFF](https://eff.org)**. This is the *[Markdown Guide](https://www.markdownguide.org)*.
additional_examples.html: I love supporting EFF. This is the Markdown Guide.

references.name: Paragraphs
references.description: To create paragraphs, use a blank line to separate one or more lines of text. You should not indent paragraphs with spaces or tabs.

examples.markdown:
I really like using Markdown.

I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.
examples.html:
I really like using Markdown.

I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on.

references.name: Task Lists
references.description: Task lists (also referred to as checklists and todo lists) allow you to create a list of items with checkboxes. In Markdown applications that support task lists, checkboxes will be displayed next to the content. To create a task list, add dashes (-) and brackets with a space ([ ]) in front of task list items. To select a checkbox, add an x in between the brackets ([x]).

examples.markdown:
- [x] Write the press release
- [ ] Update the website
- [ ] Contact the media

references.name: Unordered Lists
references.description: To create an unordered list, add dashes (`-`), asterisks (`*`), or plus signs (`+`) in front of line items. Indent one or more items to create a nested list.

references.description: Tables are created using pipes, underscored, and hyphens. Hyphens are used to separate rows, and pipes are used to separate columns.

markdowns:
# Blockquotes --- To create a blockquote, add a `>` in front of a paragraph. ## Examples --- > Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle. ## Additional Examples ## Blockquotes with Multiple Paragraphs Blockquotes can contain multiple paragraphs. Add a `>` on the blank lines between the paragraphs. > Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle. > > The Witch bade her clean the pots and kettles and sweep the floor and keep the fire fed with wood. ## Nested Blockquotes Blockquotes can be nested. Add a `>>` in front of the paragraph you want to nest. > Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle. > >> The Witch bade her clean the pots and kettles and sweep the floor and keep the fire fed with wood. ## Blockquotes with Other Elements Blockquotes can contain other Markdown formatted elements. Not all elements can be used — you'll need to experiment to see which ones work. > \#\#\# The quarterly results look great! > > \- Revenue was off the chart. > \- Profits were higher than ever. > > \*Everything\* is going according to \*\*plan\*\*. # Bold --- To bold text, add two asterisks or underscores before and after a word or phrase. To bold the middle of a word for emphasis, add two asterisks without spaces around the letters. ## Examples --- I just love \*\*bold text\*\*. I just love \_\_bold text\_\_. Love\*\*is\*\*bold # Code --- To denote a word or phrase as code, enclose it in tick marks (`` ` ``). ## Examples --- At the command prompt, type `nano`. ## Additional Examples ## Escaping Tick Marks If the word or phrase you want to denote as code includes one or more tick marks, you can escape it by enclosing the word or phrase in double tick marks (``). ``Use `code` in your Markdown file.`` ## Code Blocks To create code blocks, indent every line of the block by at least four spaces or one tab.  <html>    <head>    <\/head>  <\/html> # Headings --- To create a heading, add number signs (`#`) in front of a word or phrase. The number of number signs you use should correspond to the heading level. For example, to create a heading level three (`

`), use three number signs (e.g., `### My Header`). ## Examples --- \# Heading level 1 \#\# Heading level 2 \#\#\# Heading level 3 \#\#\#\# Heading level 4 \#\#\#\#\# Heading level 5 \#\#\#\#\#\# Heading level 6 ## Additional Examples ## Alternative H1 Syntax Alternatively, on the line below the text, add any number of == characters for heading level 1. Heading level 1 \=\=\=\=\=\=\=\=\=\=\=\=\=\=\= ## Alternative H2 Syntax Alternatively, on the line below the text, add any number of -- characters for heading level 2. Heading level 2 \-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\- # Horizontal Rules --- To create a horizontal rule, use three or more asterisks (`***`), dashes (`---`), or underscores (`___`) on a line by themselves. ## Examples --- \*\*\* \-\-\- \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ # Images --- To add an image, add an exclamation mark (`!`), followed by alt text in brackets, and the path or URL to the image asset in parentheses. You can optionally add a title after the URL in the parentheses. ## Examples --- !\[Philadelphia's Magic Gardens. This place was so cool!\]\(\/assets\/images\/philly\-magic\-gardens.jpg "Philadelphia's Magic Gardens"\) ## Additional Examples ## Linking Images To add a link to an image, enclose the Markdown for the image in brackets, and then add the link in parentheses. \[!\[An old rock in the desert\]\(\/assets\/images\/shiprock.jpg "Shiprock, New Mexico by Beau Rogers"\)\]\(https:\/\/images.unsplash.com\/photo\-1556010334\-d6ed191db491?ixlib\=rb\-1.2.1&ixid\=MnwxMjA3fDB8MHxzZWFyY2h8M3x8cm9ja3xlbnwwfHwwfHw%3D&auto\=format&fit\=crop&w\=900&q\=60\) # Italic --- To italicize text, add one asterisk or underscore before and after a word or phrase. To italicize the middle of a word for emphasis, add one asterisk without spaces around the letters. ## Examples --- Italicized text is the \*cat's meow\*. Italicized text is the \_cat's meow\_. A\*cat\*meow # Line Breaks --- To create a line break (`
`), end a line with two or more spaces, and then type return. ## Examples --- This is the first line. And this is the second line. # Links --- To create a link, enclose the link text in brackets (e.g., `[Duck Duck Go]`) and then follow it immediately with the URL in parentheses (e.g., `(https://duckduckgo.com)`). You can optionally add a title after the URL in the parentheses. ## Examples --- My favorite search engine is \[Duck Duck Go\]\(https:\/\/duckduckgo.com "The best search engine for privacy"\). ## Additional Examples ## URLs and Email Addresses To quickly turn a URL or email address into a link, enclose it in angle brackets. <https:\/\/www.markdownguide.org><fake@example.com> ## Formatting Links To emphasize links, add asterisks before and after the brackets and parentheses. I love supporting \*\*\[EFF\]\(https:\/\/eff.org\)\*\*. This is the \*\[Markdown Guide\]\(https:\/\/www.markdownguide.org\)\*. # Ordered Lists --- To create an ordered list, add line items with numbers followed by periods. The numbers don't have to be in numerical order, but the list should start with the number one. ## Examples --- 1. First item 2. Second item 3. Third item 4. Fourth item 1. First item 1. Second item 1. Third item 1. Fourth item 1. First item 8. Second item 3. Third item 5. Fourth item 1. First item 2. Second item 3. Third item 1. Indented item 2. Indented item 4. Fourth item # Paragraphs --- To create paragraphs, use a blank line to separate one or more lines of text. You should not indent paragraphs with spaces or tabs. ## Examples --- I really like using Markdown. I think I'll use it to format all of my documents from now on. # Task Lists --- Task lists (also referred to as checklists and todo lists) allow you to create a list of items with checkboxes. In Markdown applications that support task lists, checkboxes will be displayed next to the content. To create a task list, add dashes (-) and brackets with a space ([ ]) in front of task list items. To select a checkbox, add an x in between the brackets ([x]). ## Examples --- \- \[x\] Write the press release \- \[ \] Update the website \- \[ \] Contact the media # Unordered Lists --- To create an unordered list, add dashes (`-`), asterisks (`*`), or plus signs (`+`) in front of line items. Indent one or more items to create a nested list. ## Examples --- \- First item \- Second item \- Third item \- Fourth item \* First item \* Second item \* Third item \* Fourth item \+ First item \* Second item \- Third item \+ Fourth item \- First item \- Second item \- Third item     \- Indented item     \- Indented item \- Fourth item # Strikethrough --- To create a strikethrough effect, add `~~` before and directly after a block of text ## Examples --- I am ~~unable~~ able to do this! # Tables --- Tables are created using pipes, underscored, and hyphens. Hyphens are used to separate rows, and pipes are used to separate columns. ## Examples --- | Syntax | Description | | \-\-\- | \-\-\- | | Header | Title | | Paragraph | Text |
